name: Cap de Creus
description: Easternmost point of Iberian Peninsula; reference headland with multiple dive sites on its flanks

name: Farallons de Culip
description: Offshore pinnacles north of Cap de Creus; deep wall dive

name: L'Encalladora
description: Rocky point NE of Cap de Creus with walls and gorgonians

name: Massa d'Or
description: Submerged mount east of Cap de Creus; deep dive

name: Cala Jòncols
description: Sheltered cove home to Euro-Divers; shore and boat dives; Cova del Pebre is notable

name: Cala Montjoi
description: Sheltered cove south of Jòncols; Montjoi Diving Center operates here

name: La Meda
description: Islet off S'Arnella; gorgonian walls

name: Far de S'Arnella
description: Lighthouse point NE of Cadaqués

name: Cap Gros
description: Headland north of Cadaqués; wall dive

name: Cap Norfeu
description: Dramatic headland between Roses and Cala Jòncols with multiple dive sites on its flanks

name: El Portaló
description: Rocky dive site in Port de la Selva area

name: Meda Gran
description: Main island of the Medes archipelago; core of the marine reserve

name: Meda Petita
description: Smaller southern island of the Medes archipelago

name: Tascó Gros
description: Twin islet of Carall Bernat; vertical walls with red and white gorgonians

name: Tascó Petit
description: Small islet between Ferranelles and Carall Bernat; variable currents

name: Cova del Dofí (Nord)
description: North entrance of the Dolphin tunnel through Meda Petita

name: La Vaca
description: 30 m north-south tunnel through Meda Gran; 12 m entrance on south side

name: Pota del Llop
description: Deep wall on east coast of Meda Gran covered in gorgonians

name: La Reina
description: East side of Meda Gran; small cave on top of island

name: Salpatxot
description: Slope dive at north of Medes; beginner-friendly; possible moonfish in June

name: Medallot
description: Northernmost islet of the Medes group

name: Pedra de Déu
description: Submerged rock within the Medes reserve

name: Embarcador del Francès
description: North coast of Meda Gran; coral, white gorgons, nudibranchs

name: Reggio Messina
description: 122 m cargo wreck on the Montgrí coast; barracuda schools

name: Illa Pedrosa
description: Island with 60 m underwater tunnel

name: Illa Ferriola
description: Island with 25 m underwater tunnel

name: Negre del Falaguer
description: Cliff dive on the Montgrí coast

name: Punta Salines
description: Montgrí coast headland

name: Illes Formigues
description: Archipelago of 16 islets with canyons, coral, and a 1st c. BC shipwreck

name: Ullastres I
description: Inner of three submerged pinnacles off Llafranc

name: Ullastres II
description: Middle pinnacle with caves and narrow passages

name: Ullastres III
description: Outermost and deepest pinnacle; red and green gorgonians

description: Submerged seamount between Llafranc and Aiguablava; advanced dive

name: Canons de Tamariu
description: Underwater canyons off Tamariu

name: Aigua Xelida
description: Cove near Tamariu with caves and tunnels

description: 40 m former German tugboat sunk 1989; one of the most visited wrecks on the Costa Brava

name: Llosa de Palamós
description: Rocky seamount close to the Boreas wreck; all levels

name: Roca Muladera (Roca del Moro)
description: Two seamounts with a channel between; famous for light and biodiversity

name: Platja de la Falconera (Port de Garraf)
description: Shore dive; Lassdive meeting point; rocky coast stretch south of Barcelona

name: Canons de Cala Morisca
description: Canyon formations within Garraf Natural Park

name: Cala Vidre
description: Rock formations with non-accessible cavities; famed for night dives

name: Cala Forn
description: Horseshoe-shaped cove in Tres Cales; shore dive

name: Cala Llobeta
description: Shore dive with rock formations

name: Cala Sant Jordi d'Alfama
description: Next to 11th-century fortification; shore dive to 9 m

name: L'Estany
description: Shore dive with caves

name: Cala Pepo
description: Boat or shore dive

name: El Correu (Cavour)
description: Italian transatlantic liner from 1917, ~100 m long, split in two; advanced dive

name: Pepito Lalula
description: Former trawler sunk ~15 years ago; artificial reef with congers and lobsters

name: La Azur
description: 19.23 m trawler on muddy bottom; rich artificial reef

name: El Moro
description: Vessel remains sunk under EU fleet reconversion programme
